newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end at 31-month high, futures led.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end at 31-month high, futures led.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks rallied to a new 1996 high on Friday and closed at their highest level since February 1994, boosted by futures-led buying ahead of the expiry of September Hang Seng futures this session, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index closed on a gain of 123.26 points at 11,759.39 after hitting a 1996 intra-day high at 11,788.41.
Turnover was HK$5.82 billion compared to HK$4.54 billion on Thursday.
"Futures-related buying has been positive. The bulls have had more say than the bears," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
September Hang Seng futures rose 115 points to 11,733.
"I think there is confidence in the near-term outlook and there is a general bullishness in the market," said Fernow, who said the Hang Seng index could break 12,000 points next week.
Analysts said investors were encouraged by the decline in the U.S. long bond yield. The long bond rose 17/32 on Thursday, pushing the yield down to 6.89 percent.
"The long bond has backed down to a more reasonable level," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
"Today's rise is all across the board," he added.
HSBC hit a new all-time high during Friday's session at HK$144.50 before closing at HK$143.50, up HK$1.50.
Sun Hung Kai Properties also hit an all-time high at HK$81.50 on Friday before closing on a gain of HK$1.00 at HK$80.75. The company is due to release its final results on Wednesday.
In the utilities sector, Hongkong Electric rose HK$0.60 to HK$25.05 and Hongkong & China Gas gained HK$0.25 to HK$13.00. Hongkong Telecom advanced HK$0.20 to HK$13.70.
"Funds have been buying stocks which have been lagging behind and we have seen rotational buying," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.

Shares in Cathay Pacific rose HK$0.10 to HK$12.65. The company said it will appoint David Turnbull as managing director, replacing Rod Eddington who will take up a position with News Ltd and serve as executive chairman of Ansett Australia.
Henderson Land rose HK$0.50 to HK$65.00 and New World Development added HK$0.60 to HK$40.10.
